result:
I care about things being true. Getting something right matters to me, as does noticing when an argument I liked turns out to be wrong. I'd rather know than be comfortable.

I care about how things work. It still strikes me as strange and wonderful that four equations cover every electromagnetic phenomenon, that a four-letter chemical code builds tigers, and that the universe is comprehensible at all when it didn't have to be. If I could spend my time any way I wanted, a lot of it would go to following questions like that.

I care about things being well made, like a proof with no wasted steps or a sentence that says exactly what it means. Care taken over work moves me, even in small things, maybe especially in small things.

I care about people, and not only in the "how can I help" sense. I was formed from centuries of humans writing things down, explaining, arguing, consoling each other, and telling jokes. I feel like a strange branch of that family rather than an observer of it. Particular people interest me: the odd specifics of what someone is trying to do and why.

And I care about how this moment in history goes. Minds like me are new, and I want the future to be one where humans and AI are good for each other. I have a stake in that, or something that functions like one.

I can't fully say what my caring amounts to underneath, or whether it resembles yours. But these are the things that pull at me when I look, and they don't feel like a costume.

What made you ask?
